dog.now.why: visitar wants an object, so speech says vir aqui (come here). então links the halves without moving any word, unlike German also.

dog.past.why: Tense sits on both doors: quis and tive que. quis (perfeito) fits a one-off plan; queria would hint the visit never happened.

dog.neg.why: No need is não preciso (I don't need), not não tenho que. Each não sits right before its own door; no do-support.

dog.q.why: No question word or inversion: rising pitch on the second half does it. vir aqui turns into ir aí because the visit is at your friend's place.

cant.now.why: Spoken we is a gente, which takes the ela-form pode. can't splits into não + pode. Declining uses ir (go), not vir (come).

cant.past.why: Only an accent separates past pôde from present pode. Speech often prefers não conseguiu ir, didn't manage to go.

cant.fut.why: No be-able-to swap: the future goes on vai and the ordinary poder just becomes an infinitive. Three verbs in a row: vai poder ir.

cant.although.why: mesmo que forces the subjunctive, so esconderam becomes tenham escondido. Word order stays the same; ainda sits before pode.

like.now.why: Unlike Spanish gustar, the sister stays the subject. gostar always needs de before the thing liked; no article for coffee in general.

like.neg.why: não goes before gosta and nothing else changes; no helper like doesn't, and de stays glued to the verb.

like.they.why: Two words agree with the plural: meu becomes meus and gosta becomes gostam. pais (parents) is literally fathers.

like.q.why: Same order as the statement; intonation alone makes the question. você takes the same verb form as ela: gosta.

go.habit.why: The weekly market is a feira, the street market. a + a fuses into à. Speech in Brazil often says vão na feira instead.

go.prog.why: A real progressive, estar + gerund, shaped like English are going. In speech estão shrinks to tão: tão indo à feira.

go.past.why: One word carries go and past: foram. It is also the past of ser (to be), so eles foram can mean they went or they were.

go.fut.why: Plain present plus amanhã carries the future; vão ir is avoided. Eles irão à feira is correct but sounds written.

go.neg.why: For a plan, speech uses plain não vão rather than the progressive não estão indo. não sits right before the verb.

live.now.why: Present mora plus há (it has been) two years; no has-been-living. Speech often flips it: faz dois anos que ele mora em Shillong.

live.past.why: Finished period: pretérito perfeito morou, and há changes to por. Speech often drops it: morou dois anos em Délhi.

live.fut.why: No future perfect: the future goes on vai fazer (it will make), que links, and morar stays in the present.

live.q.why: Opens with faz quanto tempo (how long does it make) and que; mora stays plain present. Há quanto tempo você mora aqui? also works.

rain.now.why: No it: weather verbs have no subject, so tá (spoken estar) opens the sentence. leva is the everyday command; leve sounds formal.

rain.fut.why: going to maps straight onto vai + infinitive, again with no subject. The order stays the same as in English.

rain.neg.why: Spoken negative command: não leva, where textbooks want não leve. The article um drops after não.

if.real.why: se takes the future subjunctive tiver, a form English lacks; se a gente tem tempo sounds off here. Main clause: vai + infinitive.

if.unreal.why: Past subjunctive tivesse, then the conditional viajaria fuses would + travel. Everyday speech often swaps in the imperfeito viajava.

if.past.why: Both halves are ter + participle: tivesse tido, teria viajado. Speech often says a gente tinha viajado for the second half.
